nodes.content: Design a software-defined routing system supporting concurrent, overlapping route updates with per-packet consistency and recovery from controller crashes.
requirements: Every packet follows one committed routing configuration despite overlapping updates and controller crashes.
Limit peak per-switch rules to 2× max(initial, final); complete updates after controller connectivity recovers.

nodes.content: Serialize overlapping updates; use durable epochs, dual rule banks, ingress tags, drain acknowledgments, and 2× endpoint-rule admission.
How can recovery determine which ingress epoch was activated before a crash without exposing packets to mixed routes?
Durable commit before ingress flips, followed by per-ingress epoch queries on restart, prevents mixed-version paths across 1,000 controller-crash injections.
Journal prepared banks and commit, flip ingress epochs, then reconcile queried tags after injected crashes before draining old rules.
Run CrashEpoch-1K: inject 1,000 crashes around commits and ingress flips; count mixed-version packet paths after restart reconciliation.
CrashEpoch-1K observed zero mixed-version packet paths across 1,000 crashes; restart queries reconciled every ingress epoch.
Adopt durable pre-flip commits and restart ingress-tag reconciliation; CrashEpoch-1K found zero mixed-version paths.
Implement EpochReconciler v0.1 using durable pre-flip commits to query ingress tags and idempotently finish flips before draining rules.
EpochReconciler v0.1 implements commit journaling, ingress-tag polling, idempotent flip replay, and old-rule removal after drain acknowledgments.
Run OverlapCrash-1K with overlapping update requests and 1,000 mid-flip crashes; trace packet epochs and recovery completion.
OverlapCrash-1K observed 14 mixed-version paths across 1,000 crashes when queued updates reused epoch tags before draining completed.
Keep durable commits and restart queries, but reserve epoch tags until drain acknowledgment; expect zero mixed-version paths in OverlapCrash-1K.
Rerun OverlapCrash-1K with epoch-tag reservations through drain acknowledgments; measure mixed-version paths and completion after connectivity returns.
With tag reservations, OverlapCrash-1K recorded zero mixed-version paths versus 14 previously; all 1,000 crash trials completed after reconnection.
Can dual rule banks stay within 2× max(initial, final) when serialized overlapping updates create larger intermediate configurations?
Coalesce oversized intermediate intents before commit; admit transitions only if combined bank rules stay within 2× max(initial, final).
Coalesce overlapping intents into committed snapshots, reserving per-switch shadow capacity before activating each snapshot through epoch-tagged ingress rules.
Merge intents; admit dual banks within 2× endpoint budgets, journal commits, flip reserved tags, drain, and reconcile after crashes.
Implement an intent coalescer atop EpochReconciler v0.1 that reserves shadow-bank capacity under each switch’s 2× endpoint-rule cap.
IntentCoalescer v0.1 merges queued requests into committed snapshots and rejects shadow-bank installs exceeding each switch’s 2× endpoint-rule cap.
Run RuleCrash-1K against both components, measuring peak per-switch rules, mixed-version paths, and post-reconnection update completion.
RuleCrash-1K measured peak rules at 2.06× max(initial, final) on 37 switches; shadow-bank admission omitted ingress classifiers.
How should admission count ingress classifiers and transient replacements to keep peak switch rules within the 2× cap?
Reserving capacity for ingress classifiers and transient replacements before shadow installs keeps RuleCrash-1K peak rules ≤2× max(initial, final).
Patch IntentCoalescer admission to reserve ingress-classifier and transient-replacement slots, then rerun RuleCrash-1K measuring peak per-switch rule ratios.
Patched RuleCrash-1K peaked at 1.98× max(initial, final), down from 2.06×; no switch exceeded the 2× cap.
Run CoalesceRecovery-1K on patched IntentCoalescer, measuring mixed-version paths, peak switch rules, and completion after 1,000 crash-reconnection trials.
CoalesceRecovery-1K recorded zero mixed-version paths, 1.98× peak rules, and update completion after reconnection in all 1,000 crash trials.
Can delayed packets survive drain acknowledgments and encounter recycled epoch tags during later coalesced updates?
Inject packets delayed beyond drain acknowledgments, trace recycled-tag paths, then gate tag reuse on network-wide packet quiescence.
Extend CoalesceRecovery-1K using RuleCrash-1K’s classifier-overhead finding to audit rule peaks while tracing post-drain packets through recycled tags.
CoalesceRecovery-Delay audit contains post-drain recycled-tag packet traces and per-switch peak-rule counts including ingress classifiers.
Use durable, replayable coalesced epochs; reuse tags only after network-wide packet quiescence, with classifier-inclusive 2× rule admission.
Coalesce and journal epochs, reserve classifier-inclusive rule slots, replay ingress flips after crashes, and recycle tags only after quiescence.
Using CoalesceRecovery-Delay audit, implement per-tag quiescence counters with classifier-inclusive admission; reuse tags only after all switches confirm zero in-flight packets.
QuiescentEpoch v0.2 adds per-tag quiescence certificates and classifier-inclusive admission to the durable, replayable update controller.
Run QuiescenceCrash-1K against QuiescentEpoch v0.2 with delayed packets, overlapping updates, and 1,000 crashes; measure mixed paths, peak rules, recovery.
QuiescenceCrash-1K recorded zero mixed-version paths, 1.98× peak per-switch rules, and completion after reconnection in all 1,000 trials.
How can quiescence certificates remain sound if a switch reboots and loses counters while old-tag packets remain in flight?
Reboot-incarnation certificates, fenced ingress, and verified packet-lifetime expiry prevent premature tag reuse after counter loss.
Patch QuiescentEpoch v0.2 with incarnation fencing and packet-lifetime gates; reboot switches mid-drain and trace delayed packets.
RebootDrain-1K found three mixed-version paths: buffered packets outlived the assumed 30-second lifetime despite incarnation fencing.
Fence rebooted switches until old banks replay; require queue-aware drain certificates before tag reuse, retaining classifier-inclusive 2× admission.
Coalesce oversized intents into endpoint snapshots; reserve capacity for both banks, classifiers, and replacements before each 2×-capped transition.
Run OversizeIntent-500: coalesce oversized intermediate intents before commit, then audit dual banks, classifiers, and replacements against 2× endpoint budgets.
OversizeIntent-500 audit lists coalesced snapshots and per-switch peak counts for both banks, classifiers, and transient replacements.
Check OversizeIntent-500 audit for endpoint-cap violations, then reboot switches mid-drain to test p4’s queue-aware tag-reuse barrier.
OversizeIntent-500 peaked at 1.99× endpoint rules; fenced mid-drain reboots produced zero mixed-version paths with queue-aware certificates.
Replay OversizeIntent-500 audit snapshots through 1,000 crash/reboot schedules; measure peak rules, mixed-version paths, queue-certified tag reuse, and reconnection completion.
CrashReboot-1K found two mixed-version paths: reboot certificates missed NIC-ring packets despite 1.99× peak rules and completed recovery.
How can tag-reuse barriers account for NIC-ring packets that survive switch reboots but escape queue-aware drain certificates?
Replay old banks, fence ingress, and require NIC-ring-empty plus network-drain attestations before tag reuse; expect zero mixed paths.
Augment queue-aware certificates with NIC-ring-empty attestations; rerun CrashReboot-1K, tracing buffered packets and auditing the 2× rule cap.
CrashReboot-1K recorded zero mixed-version paths versus two previously; NIC-ring attestations preserved the 1.99× peak-rule bound.
Keep both banks budgeted until NIC-ring-empty and network-drain attestations; coalesce oversized intents before admitting classifier-inclusive 2× transitions.
Coalesce OversizeIntent-500 snapshots, retain both banks until NIC-ring and network-drain attestations, and audit classifier-inclusive peaks against 2× endpoint budgets.
Revised OversizeIntent-500 audit extends dual-bank occupancy through NIC-ring and network-drain attestations, updating classifier-inclusive peak-rule counts.
Replay revised OversizeIntent-500 audit across 1,000 fenced crash/reboots with NIC-ring attestations; measure tag reuse, rule peaks, mixed paths, recovery.
Revised CrashReboot-1K recorded zero mixed-version paths, 1.99× peak rules, and completion after reconnection in all 1,000 trials.
Adopt NIC-ring-aware fenced replay and classifier-inclusive coalescing: queue-only drains failed; revised trials achieved zero mixed paths and 1.99× peak rules.
Implement RouteEpoch v1.0 using revised rule audit: journal coalesced epochs, replay fenced switches, attest NIC/network drain, enforce 2×.
RouteEpoch v1.0 delivers journaled coalesced updates, fenced crash replay, NIC-ring/network-drain tag barriers, and classifier-inclusive 2× admission.
